title: Backtracking

views.title: Backtracking
views.intro: Choose, explore, undo. Subsets and combinations move a START index forward; permutations use a used[] array. For duplicate inputs sort first and skip equal siblings at the same depth. Prune early with a cheap feasibility bound.
table: used[] array, with duplicate skip rule
N-Queens, sudoku with occupancy sets or bitmasks

files.desc: Subsets (+dup), permutations (+unique), combinations, combination sum I/II, parentheses, phone, palindrome partition, word search, N-Queens, sudoku, IP addresses, add operators, gray code

pitfalls: Add a COPY of the current path to the result, not the live list.
Duplicates: `i > start && a[i] == a[i-1]` for combinations; `used[i-1]` check for permutations.
Prune before recursing (remaining sum < 0, not enough elements left) instead of after.

decisions.a: Track counts, only add legal characters
Occupancy sets / bitmasks for O(1) validity

decisions.q: Find a path of letters in a grid?
decisions.a: Mark visited in place, restore on exit

calibration: SDE2 bar: subsets, permutations, combination sum, generate parentheses, letter combinations, word search.
SDE3 bar: duplicate handling, palindrome partitioning, N-Queens, sudoku solver, restore IP addresses, expression add operators.
Staff bar (for context): pruning heuristics, bitmask-based constraint propagation, and recognizing when DP or meet-in-the-middle replaces brute force.
